translations.title: Rhyme XXXI: Our passion was a tragic farce
translations.text:
Our passion was a tragic farce

in whose absurd fable

the comic and the grave, confused,

drew laughter and tears.


But worst of all that story

was that, at the end of the play,

tears and laughter fell to her,

and to me only tears!
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly from the supplied Spanish text; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Rhyme LXIV: As a Miser Guards His Treasure
translations.text:
As a miser guards his treasure,
I guarded my pain;
I wanted to prove something could last forever
to her who swore her love for me would never end.

But today I call to it in vain, and hear time,
which wore it away, say:
“Ah, wretched clay, you cannot
even suffer forever!”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XCI: The Sun May Be Clouded Forever
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXXVI: If the Story of Our Wrongs Were Written
translations.text:
If the story of our wrongs
were written in a book,
and all that was erased from its pages
were erased from our souls,

I love you still so much; your love
left such deep traces in my breast,
that if you erased just one,
I would erase them all!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLIV: As in an Open Book
translations.text:
As in an open book,
I read what lies deep in your eyes;
why should your lips feign laughter
that your eyes deny?

Weep! Do not be ashamed
to admit you loved me a little.
Weep! No one is watching us.
You see, I am a man... and I weep too!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XLVII: I Have Peered into the Deep Chasms
translations.text:
I have peered into the deep chasms
of earth and heaven,
and have seen where they end, whether with my eyes
or with my mind.

But alas, I came to the abyss of a heart
and leaned over to see it,
and my soul and eyes grew troubled:
it was so deep and so dark!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LIV: When We Recall the Fleeting Hours
translations.text:
When we turn back to recall
the fleeting hours of the past,
a tear trembles on her dark lashes,
ready to slip away.

And at last it slips and falls like a drop
of dew, as she thinks
that, as today we sigh for yesterday,
tomorrow we both will sigh for today.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme XXXII: She Passed, Overwhelming in Her Beauty
translations.text:
She passed, overwhelming in her beauty,
and I let her go by;
I did not even turn to look, and yet
something whispered in my ear: “That is she.”

Who joined evening to morning?
I do not know; I know only
that in one brief summer night
the twilights met, and... “it happened.”
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXXXVI: Like a Lost Sailor, I Sought Refuge
translations.text:
Like a lost sailor, I sought refuge
in a woman and asked her for love;
her love wearied my senses
and froze my heart.

And along the course of my life,
which yesterday held a world of hope,
I was left like a traveler in the desert:
alone with God!
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme LXIII: Like a Swarm of Angry Bees
translations.text:
Like a swarm of angry bees,
memories of the hours gone by
emerge from a dark corner of memory
to pursue me.

I try to drive them away. A useless effort!
They surround me, harry me,
and one after another come to pierce me
with a sharp sting that inflames my soul.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Rhyme L: What the Savage Does with His Clumsy Hands
translations.text:
What the savage does when his clumsy hands
fashion a god from a tree trunk at his whim
and then kneel before his work,
that is what you and I did.

We gave real shape to a phantom,
a foolish invention of the mind,
and once the idol was made, we sacrificed
our love upon its altar.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
